title: Greedy-windowed KV-slim batcher for low-jitter streaming completions
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Streaming chat workloads show spiky turn arrivals and highly variable token lengths. Our current continuous batcher can either favor throughput (large batches) or latency (small batches) but struggles when KV cache memory pressure forces eviction mid-turn, which causes jitter and tail latency spikes. Goal: introduce a lightweight, memory-aware batching heuristic that packs streaming turns greedily into a short sliding window while applying on-the-fly KV-slim transformations to older session KV entries so we can keep more sessions hot on GPU without increasing P95 latency.

Scope: deliver a new batch formation policy (runtime pluggable) + KV-slimmer module + GPU slab reservation adjustments for streaming completions. This ticket covers design, prototype, unit and perf tests, and a canary rollout in a test shard. Integration with the existing continuous batching runtime and fallback to current policy required.
acceptance_criteria: New batcher policy available behind flag and selectable per-model-route
P95 generation latency for 90th percentile sessions improves or remains within 5% of baseline for short-turn workloads
Median token throughput improves for mixed-length streaming traffic by >=8% relative to baseline under same GPU config
KV cache eviction rate reduced for top-1000 sessions in canary shard by >=20%
No increase in OOM incidents in dedicated canary cluster; any memory pressure triggers safe fallback to legacy policy
End-to-end integration tests and load tests cover edge cases (session churn, long-turns, preemptions)
implementation_notes:
Design summary: implement a greedy-windowed packer that maintains a short time window (configurable, default 40ms) and a per-GPU soft memory budget. Incoming streaming turns enter a lightweight priority queue keyed by (deadline, session_hotness_score). The packer greedily forms batches by selecting turns that fit the current GPU slab budget. If budget is near limit, it invokes KV-slimmer on the session with oldest inactive bytes: KV-slimmer applies two transformations in order - 1) LZ4-ranged compact (lossless) to long inactive KV segments and 2) 8-bit delta quantization for frozen KV arrays where model-compatibility tests pass. These transforms are fast (<1ms typical) and can be offloaded to async CPU threadpool; the packer accounts for transform latency in its window. GPU slab reservation: reserve a small spill slab (default 6% of GPU memory) for mid-batch growth to avoid mid-batch OOM; if slab usage exceeds threshold, mark batch as high-risk and reduce target batch-size. Pluggable via RuntimeConfig.batch_policy = "greedy_windowed_kv_slim".

Data structures: per-session hotness score maintained in LRU-ish structure decayed by activity. KV metadata stores last_access_ts, compressed_size hints, and quantization_eligibility flags. All KV-slim operations produce metadata for safe rollbacks.

Trade-offs: aggressive slimming increases risk of minor quality shifts for sessions that later resume long-turn generations; to mitigate we only quantize frozen KV segments (no active KV) and maintain original KV on CPU disk for quick restore in rare cases. The chosen greedy approach prioritizes low jitter for live sessions at modest throughput cost compared to large-batch modes.
testing_plan:
Unit tests for packer selection logic, kv-slimmer correctness, rollback paths, and slab reservation accounting. Integration tests: simulated streaming driver that emits Poisson turn arrivals with mixed length distributions (short bursts, long monologues). Perf runs: run A/B on canary cluster for 72h with traffic replay from production traces (anonymized) to measure p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, and memory churn. OOM-injection tests: artificially reduce GPU memory to validate safe fallback. Quality validation: automated eval set to check for output regressions after KV-slim quantization on representative prompts.

Test artifacts: load test harness scripts, synthetic traffic configs, and evaluation prompts stored under docs/perf/greedy-windowed-2026-03 in Confluence.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag gated internal smoke (dev cluster). Phase 1: Canary in two low-traffic runtime shards for 72h with observability and auto-rollback on OOM or latency regression. Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 10% of streaming traffic with monitoring thresholds. Phase 3: Full release and default opt-in for streaming routes. Rollout will include an emergency kill switch and auto-fallback to legacy policy.
observability: Add metrics: batcher.window_fill_ratio, batcher.average_pack_latency_ms, kv_slim.operations.count, kv_slim.avg_latency_ms, slab_spill.bytes, slab_spill.incidents, per_route.p95_stream_latency. Add traces for batch formation path and kv-slim decisions (sampled). Dashboards: streaming_batcher_overview and kv_slim_health. Alerts: p95_stream_latency > baseline + 15% for 10m, slab_spill.incidents > 5 in 5m, kv_slim.error_rate >1%.
performance_targets: Target p95 stream generation latency: <= baseline +5% under median load. Token throughput: +8% median for mixed workloads in canary. KV eviction reduction: -20% top sessions. CPU overhead for kv-slim: <= 3% of worker CPU across shard. Transform tail latency: 99th percentile < 10ms.
risks: 1) KV quantization may introduce subtle model output shifts for rare long resumption cases. Mitigation: conservative eligibility checks and restore-from-CPU path. 2) CPU-side kv-slim overhead may compete with other background work. Mitigation: bounded threadpool and backpressure to packer. 3) Complexity in rollback under multi-shard session migration; mitigation: versioned KV metadata and idempotent operations.
next_steps: 1) Finalize canary config knobs (window_ms, soft_memory_budget, slab_spill_pct). 2) Land packer prototype PR and kv-slimmer PR in staging. 3) Run 72h canary with production trace replay. 4) Iterate on thresholds and expand rollout.
comments: 2026-03-02: Spike completed — prototype packer shows 6.5% throughput improvement on synthetic mixed workload. CPU cost for kv-slim ~2.1% in tests.
2026-03-04: Design review with ML and Infra; agreed to restrict quantization to inactive KV segments and keep original KV offloaded to CPU for 2 minutes before evicting.
2026-03-07: Implemented basic rollback and metadata versioning; unit tests added for idempotent kv-slim operations.
2026-03-10: Integration load run found rare mid-batch slab_spill during synthetic spike; increased spill slab to 6% and added high-risk batch marking logic.
2026-03-13: Canary PRs opened and awaiting infra review for canary shard allocation.
